CVE-2026-57914 is a stack overflow on deeply nested ASN.1 input in Apache Kerby, fixed in Kerby 2.1.2. The kerby-asn1 1.0.1 classes reported here are shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6 in the druid-ranger-security extension and cannot be upgraded on their own. The latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) carries kerby-asn1 2.0.3 and no Kerby 2.1.2 copy. The shaded ASN.1 parser can be reached when the Hadoop client handles Kerberos data in a secured deployment, so reachability has not been ruled out. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x6vc-x4v4-hjhr

CVE-2026-102554 is fixed in Guava 33.7.2. The Guava copies reported here are embedded inside other jars and cannot be upgraded on their own: 14.0.1 inside ambari-metrics-common 2.7.0.0.0 (ambari-metrics-emitter extension), 30.1.1-jre shaded inside hadoop-client-runtime 3.3.6, and 33.2.1-jre (Druid 36) or 33.4.8-jre (Druid 37) inside iceberg-bundled-guava (druid-iceberg-extensions). The latest Iceberg release (iceberg-bundled-guava 1.12.0) still bundles Guava 33.7.1-jre, and the latest hadoop-client-runtime (3.5.0) bundles 33.4.8-jre. The issue requires Java deserialization of an attacker-crafted CompactHashMap, CompactHashSet or MapMakerInternalMap stream; reachability through these extensions has not been assessed. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94

Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Druid does not instantiate or expose a JLine Telnet server; jline is bundled as a transitive dependency (via the org.jline:jline uber-jar) for CLI line-reading only. The telnet server code is present in the uber-jar but is never loaded or executed in Druid's runtime. The fix exists only in jline 4.x (all 3.x versions are affected) and upgrading is a major version change incompatible with the current dependency tree.
